SubProcess

General Concept: A SubProcess in BPMN is a process element that contains a set of activities, events, and gateways grouped together. It helps organize complex workflows into manageable units and can be expanded or collapsed in diagrams.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, a SubProcess is executed as part of the parent process. It has its own scope for variables, events, and error handling. Input and output mappings can be defined using FEEL expressions. SubProcesses support boundary events, multi-instance execution, and error propagation. Variable scoping ensures isolation between parent and subprocess unless explicitly mapped.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
A SubProcess in TaktX allows you to:

  • Run embedded workflows within a parent process, with their own lifecycle and variable scope.
  • Configure input and output mappings using FEEL expressions for flexible data transformation.
  • Encapsulate a set of activities as a subprocess for modular design.
  • Set up error handling, compensation, and boundary events for robust process control.
  • Monitor execution and audit results via the TaktX client.

 

Example: Order Fulfillment with Subprocess

 

This example shows a process where a Subprocess is used for order fulfillment, encapsulating multiple steps such as picking, packing, and shipping. The Subprocess demonstrates modular process design and encapsulation of related activities.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use SubProcesses to modularize and clarify complex workflows.
  • Attach boundary events for error handling and timeouts.
  • Use input/output mappings to control data flow between parent and subprocess.
  • Document the purpose and expected outcomes of each SubProcess.

Pitfalls:

  • Unmapped variables will not be visible in the subprocess.
  • Uncaught errors in the subprocess can terminate the parent process.
  • Complex subprocesses can be hard to maintain.
